source.title: Free Boundary Minimal Surfaces in the Unit Ball: Recent Advances and Open Questions

accepted.question_text: Let Σ be a k-dimensional manifold, possibly immersed or embedded, inside the Euclidean unit ball B^n, with boundary on ∂B^n, such that Σ is minimal and meets ∂B^n orthogonally along its boundary; in other words, Σ is a free boundary minimal submanifold in B^n. What topological restrictions, if any, must Σ satisfy in order for such a free boundary minimal submanifold to exist? In particular, does the answer depend on whether one asks for immersed examples or embedded examples?
accepted.context_brief: Topology of free boundary minimal submanifolds

evidence.quote: Open Question 1. Are there any topological obstructions for a k-dimension submanifold Σ to be a free boundary minimal submanifold in B^n? Does it depend on whether Σ is immersed or embedded?

An immersed (resp. embedded) submanifold ϕ : Σ^k → B^n with ϕ(∂Σ) ⊂ ∂B^n is said to be an immersed (resp. embedded) free boundary minimal submanifold if both of the following holds: (i) Σ is a minimal submanifold (ii) Σ meets ∂B^n orthogonally along ∂Σ.

accepted.question_text: Fix a compact surface Σ with boundary and a prescribed topological type, and let g range over smooth Riemannian metrics on Σ. For each positive integer k, what is the exact sharp upper bound of the normalized k-th Steklov eigenvalue σ_k(g)|∂Σ|_g for that topological type? Moreover, is this sharp upper bound attained by some smooth metric on Σ rather than only as a supremum over metrics?

evidence.quote: Open Question 2 (Fraser-Schoen [30]). For each topological type of Σ, what is the sharp upper bound for σ_k(g)|∂Σ|_g? Is it achieved by a smooth metric on Σ?
These are called the Steklov eigenvalues of (Σ, g).

accepted.question_text: For each positive integer p, let ω_p(B^n) denote the p-width of the unit ball and let Σ_p be a smooth embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface in B^n, with multiplicity n_p, such that ω_p(B^n) = n_p|Σ_p|. Must the family {Σ_p}_{p∈N} contain infinitely many distinct hypersurfaces? If it does, must their areas satisfy |Σ_p| → +∞ as p → ∞?

evidence.quote: for each p ∈ N, there exists a smooth embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface Σ_p in B^n and a positive integer n_p ∈ N such that (3.2) ω_p(B^n) = n_p|Σ_p|.
Open Question 3. Is {Σ_p}_{p∈N} an infinite set? If so, does |Σ_p| → +∞ as p → ∞?

accepted.question_text: For sufficiently large genus g, there are two families of embedded free boundary minimal surfaces in B^3 described in the survey: the desingularization examples Σ_g^{KL} and the equivariant min-max examples Σ_g^K, each having genus g, three boundary components, and the same dihedral symmetry. For all sufficiently large g, are these two surfaces actually congruent to one another, meaning the same surface up to rigid motions of B^3?

evidence.quote: Open Question 4. For all g sufficiently large, are the surfaces Σ_g^{KL} and Σ_g^K congruent to each other?
Given that the topology and the symmetry group are the same as those constructed in Theorem 3.9, it is reasonable to ask the following:

accepted.question_text: In the three-dimensional unit ball B^3, is every embedded free boundary minimal annulus congruent, up to rigid motions of B^3, to the critical catenoid? Equivalently, is the critical catenoid the unique embedded free boundary minimal annulus in B^3?

evidence.quote: Open Question 5. Is the critical catenoid the only (up to rigid motions in B^3) embedded free boundary minimal annulus in B^3?
We call K^{n−1} the (n − 1)-dimensional critical catenoid. When n = 3, we simply call it the critical catenoid denoted by K.

accepted.question_text: Among all immersed free boundary minimal surfaces in the three-dimensional unit ball B^3, is the critical catenoid the only one whose Morse index is equal to 4, up to rigid motions of B^3?

evidence.quote: Open Question 6. Is the critical catenoid the only (up to rigid motions) immersed free boundary minimal surface in B^3 with Morse index 4?
Theorem 5.5 (Tran [100], Smith-Zhou [96], Devyver [19]). The Morse index of the critical catenoid K in B^3 is equal to 4.

accepted.question_text: Let Σ be an embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface in the Euclidean unit ball B^n. Since the coordinate functions restricted to Σ are Steklov eigenfunctions with eigenvalue 1, one always has σ_1(Σ) ≤ 1. Must the first nonzero Steklov eigenvalue actually satisfy the sharp equality σ_1(Σ) = 1 for every such embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface?

evidence.quote: Open Question 7. If Σ ⊂ B^n is an embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface, then σ_1(Σ) = 1.
Recall that the coordinate functions of R^n restricted to a free boundary minimal submanifold Σ^k ⊂ B^n are Steklov eigenfunctions with Steklov eigenvalue 1. Therefore, σ_1(Σ) ≤ 1.

accepted.question_text: Let Σ^k be an immersed free boundary minimal submanifold of the Euclidean unit ball B^n, and let f: B^n → B^n be a conformal diffeomorphism. Is the k-dimensional volume of Σ maximal within its conformal orbit, in the sense that the inequality |f(Σ)| ≤ |Σ| always holds?

evidence.quote: Open Question 8. Let Σ^k be an immersed free boundary minimal submanifold in B^n, and f : B^n → B^n be a conformal diffeomorphism. Is it true that |f(Σ)| ≤ |Σ|?

accepted.question_text: Let Σ^k be an immersed free boundary minimal submanifold of the Euclidean unit ball B^n, and let f: B^n → B^n be a conformal diffeomorphism. Is the (k−1)-dimensional volume of the boundary maximal within its conformal orbit, in the sense that |f(∂Σ)| ≤ |∂Σ| always holds?

evidence.quote: Open Question 9. Let Σ^k be an immersed free boundary minimal submanifold in B^n. Suppose f : B^n → B^n is a conformal diffeomorphism. Is it true that |f(∂Σ)| ≤ |∂Σ|?

accepted.question_text: Let Σ be an immersed free boundary minimal surface in the three-dimensional unit ball B^3, and assume Σ is not an equatorial disk. Must its area be at least the area of the critical catenoid K? Equivalently, is the critical catenoid the next smallest-area example after the equatorial disk among immersed free boundary minimal surfaces in B^3?

evidence.quote: Open Question 10. Let Σ^2 be an immersed free boundary minimal surface in B^3 which is not the equatorial disk. Is it true that |Σ| ≥ |K|?
When n = 3, we simply call it the critical catenoid denoted by K.
